msContents.summary: [p]Commonplace book, containing notes on philosophy, logic, grammar, literary composition, Latin verses, sermons, etc.: including a transcript of the 'Ars memorativa' by Jacobus Publicius, and an incomplete Latin-German Glossary of Herbs, etc.: in Latin.[/p] [p]Two leaves are wanting between fol. 76 and fol. 77, and one leaf after ff. 21, 151: the end of the Glossary after P is missing. [/p] [p]Some headings, etc. are in cypher: a key to which has been inserted. [/p] [p]Some initials, paragraph marks, headings, and underlinings in red. [/p] [p]On fol. 7 is a rough pen-drawing of the Cosmos over a crude map of the earth, and on fol. 18v a chess-board of 64 squares, on fol. 31v a diagram illustrating the syllogism. On fol. 68 is a note of books lent by an early 17th cent. owner. On fol. 121 is an impression of a seal, the details of which are obscure, but it is lettered G. H. On the first leaf is the signature of Alessandro Padoani [c. 1600?]. [/p] [p]No. 1, the 'Ars memorativa' was first printed at Venice in 1482. [/p] [p]Produced in Freiburg.[/p] [li]Publicius, F. Ars memorativa: Fol. 1 (red) Ars memorie [Jacobi Publi / cii Florentini (in cypher)] Incipit feliciter / Et primo prefacio. / HAud ab re fore arbitror si preter / maiorum consuetudinem ... 18 ...et rotundum cum / laude fructum auditores nostri inde consequi / valeant et illis deo se commendant.[/li][li][Anon.] De memoria: Fol. 19 (red) Alia opinio de memoria nuper / compilata a reuerendo [Patre quodam cartusiano (in cypher)] freiburgense in similitudine commedie colloquuntur magister et discipuli. / MEmorie nunc ordo precepta / ministrat (inquit magister) ... 25v (red) Raptim ut uentus. 22 Notes on memory. 23, 24 Notes on logic. 25 Blank. 26 Notes on logic.[/li][li]Burley, W. On logic: extracts: Fol. 27 LOgica est ars arcium scientia / scientiarum ... 60v sed intelligas quid a decipere conante cauendum sit. / TELOS. 61-67 Notes and extracts on Logic: perhaps also from Burley. 68v-70 Blank. 71-75 Notes and extracts 'De anima', and on Logic. 76 Blank.[/li][li][Anon.] Short work on logic: Fol. 77 Vtrum proprium et accidens sint predica / bilia ab aliis. 86 ...Quarta est facilitas soluendi / per silogismos probantes in forma vtili [?].[/li][li][Anon.] De prophecia et prophetis: Fol. 87 Prophetia prophetes prophetis ... 92v ...que deo displiceant / et scripturam (?) abominat anima eius.[/li][li]B. H. Sermo: Fol. 93 (red) Sermo in vigilia profesti nativitatis domini / super verbo ihesu christi filii dei in / bethleem iudeae nationis per magistrum h. / b. augustinorum religiosum in freiburgo factus. 96 ...Dixi. precate pro me / (red) anno 1515. 97-98 Sermons. 99, 100 Blank.[/li][li][Anon.] Work on Grammar: Fol. 101-103 GRammatica est ars recte loquendi / recteque scribendi...[/li][li]S. Anthonius, De arte metrificandi: Fol. 103v De arte metrificandi [Anthonii S. (in cypher)]. / Cum ygitur destinatum est de partibus illis / ex quibus carmina ... 106v, line 14 ...adhuc mille precepta carminibus considerandis dici potest.[/li][li]Latin verses by Hasius: Fol. 106v, line 15-Fol 110v Ff. 111-115 Blank. Fol. 115v Notes on the Sibyls. 116v Poem by Hasius: with a note partly in cypher: 'Frater Gregorius Hasius composuit carmina anno 1515 circa vendimiale septimum' in red. 117 Verses on the Seasons, Months, Temperaments, etc. 118 Metrical memoranda on feast-days beginning: 'Cisio Janus epique...'.[/li][li]Spenlin (Georgius), Epistola: Ff. 119, 120 [Frater georgius studens Wittembur / gensis ita scribit priorato suo / : in cypher]. It is signed at the end, also in cypher 'Georgius Spenlin'.[/li][li]Hasius, G., Epistola commendatoria: Fol. 120, line 8 [Litterae testimoniales Augusti fratris / ordinis minorum de argentina studentis: in cypher]. / ... The letter is addressed to 'Melchior Fabri diacono et arcium professori solerti ordinum minorum' by Hasius who describes himself as 'Sacre theologie professor'. It is dated at Strassburg, February 1515. (Fol. 121).[/li][li]Aegidius de Viterbo. Copy of a letter: Fol. 122 Letter to Theophilus Neapolitanus, dated 1515.[/li][li]Hasius, G. Two latin orations: Ff. 122v-127 128, 129 Notes on Logic. 130-133 Blank.[/li][li][Anon.] Ars epistolandi: Fol. 134 De quibusdam eleganciis epistolarum. Ff.Ff. 135-151 De quibusdam dictionibus et earum quantitatibus contra morem generaliter loquentem. 152-156 Notes on the Aeneid. 156v, 157 Blank.[/li][li][Anon.] Latin-German glossary of herbs. In double column, incomplete: Fol. 158, col. 1 Apium vulgo epse / ... 162v, col. 2 Picaria nacht und tag. 163 Notes on sermons.[/li]
